extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent applicants (Korea; foreign applicants seeking to understand KIPO practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Official, comprehensive examination guidelines from the Korean Intellectual Property Office (Dec 2017) that define procedural rules, formal requirements, patentability standards (novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability), amendment practice, examination procedures, and technology-specific examination criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines who may file or conduct patent-related proceedings (e.g., legal capacity of minors, persons under guardianship, unincorporated associations, overseas residents), and the effect of treaties on capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes Article 3 (Legal Capacity of Minors, etc.), Article 4 (Unincorporated Associations), Article 5 (Patent Administrators for Overseas Residents) and Article 25 (Capacity of Foreigners to Hold Rights). Explains when representation by a legal representative or patent administrator is required and scope of their authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agents (Representation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and categories for representation in patent proceedings: legal representative, contractual representative, patent administrator, appointment/replacement and other representation provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers overview of representation, legal vs contractual representatives, patent administrator duties, procedures for appointment or replacement, and additional provisions governing agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periods (deadlines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of procedural periods, methods to calculate periods, and rules for extension of periods relevant to patent proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies types of periods, calculation rules, extension procedures and any special considerations for computing and extending statutory deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidation of Proceeding and Return of Document
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and procedures for formalities examination, invalidation of proceedings, revocation of invalidation, return of documents, subsequent completion of proceedings, and restoration of patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes general principles of formality examination, grounds and procedures for invalidation and revival, and rules for returning documents and restoring applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discontinuation and Resumption of Proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for discontinuing proceedings, conditions for resumption, continuation of proceedings and succession of effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies when proceedings are considered discontinued, how to continue or resume proceedings, and legal effects of discontinuation and continuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission and Service of Documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements and procedures for submission and service of documents in patent-related proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers how documents must be submitted, served, and any formal requirements (format, timing, recipient), plus service-related procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees (payment, reduction, refund)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements and procedures for payment of patent and official fees, rules for fee reduction and refund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details payment methods, eligibility and processes for fee reduction, and conditions and procedures to obtain refunds of fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Patent-Related Proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures governing inspection of documents, prohibition of documents being taken out or laid open to the public, referencing documents, and offenses relating to divulging confidential information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies inspection rights, confidentiality protections, referencing of documents, and criminal/administrative sanctions for unauthorized disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Application (formal and substantive parts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements relating to patent applications including inventor identification, successor in title, protection of legitimate right holders, and references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes who must be named, rights of successors, protections for legitimate holders, and how references are to be treated in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Application Documents (cover sheet, abstract, specification, drawings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Content and formal requirements for application documents: application cover sheet, abstract, full specification, and drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies what each document must contain, formatting and content guidance (e.g., abstract conventions, specification organization, required drawings) and how these documents support examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of Invention — Enablement Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that the specification enable a person skilled in the art to carry out the invention (enablement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes what level of detail is required, examples of sufficient/insufficient disclosure, and cross-references to description method requirements and background-art description obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description Method Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: How the invention and its embodiments must be described in the specification (structure, examples, best mode where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers organizational method, necessary elements to be described, how to disclose embodiments, and instructions on avoiding new matter or vague language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for Description of Background Art
rubrics_metrics.description: Obligation to describe relevant background art and to identify the problem(s) to be solved by the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains what background art should be included, how to present prior art, and how to frame the technical problem in the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims — Recognition and Support by Description
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must be supported by and be recognizable from the description; claims must not claim matter not disclosed in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes 'claims supported by description of invention' — examiners assess whether claims are adequately disclosed and justified by the specification; cross-reference to added-matter/amendment rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims — Clear and Concise Statement of Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must be clear, concise and define the matter for which protection is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on drafting for clarity, avoiding ambiguous terminology, properly defining technical features and boundaries of the claimed subject-matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims — Matters Necessary for Specification of Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain matters are deemed necessary to specify an invention within claims (e.g., essential technical features).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner instructions on what technical details are considered necessary to include in the claims to properly specify the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims — Claim Drafting Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal and substantive requirements for claim drafting (dependent/independent claims, numbering, antecedent basis, allowable amendments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical drafting rules, examples of acceptable claim formats, and cautionary notes regarding improper amendments and added matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: System for Deferral of Submission of Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules allowing deferral of claim submission under certain conditions and procedures governing such deferral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When and how claims may be deferred, effects on examination, and procedural steps required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles for determining whether a set of claims constitutes a single inventive concept (unity), including general considerations and special cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on purpose of unity requirement, methods of determination, examples, special cases, and examiner instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications Related to Microorganisms (deposit system and sequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special rules for applications involving microorganisms, including deposit requirements, application procedures, and instructions on exam for nucleic acid/amino acid sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers deposit system details, how to handle sequence listings, and specific examination guidance for biological materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial Applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that the invention be capable of industrial application; purport, statutory inventions and identification of industrially inapplicable inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains scope of industrial applicability, examples of inapplicable inventions, and how to evaluate this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty requirement (Article references), understanding of statutory provisions, determination of novelty and disclosure exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner methods to assess whether claimed subject-matter is new over prior art, treatment of disclosure exceptions, and standards of identicalness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive Step (non-obviousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and methods for determining inventive step including definitions, general principles, methods of determination, concrete methods, treatment of combination inventions and other relevant factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides stepwise methods for inventive-step analysis: identify closest prior art, determine differences and technical effect, consider common general knowledge and motivation to combine, evaluate whether reasoning from prior art to claimed invention is available to a person skilled in the art. If such reasoning exists, inventive step is denied; if not, inventive step is acknowledged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive Step — Computer-related inventions (specific guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special considerations when assessing inventive step for computer-related inventions: evaluate closest prior art, problems to be solved (software-implementation/computerization), ordinary skill in the art, and ordinary creative activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Key points and examples from the guidelines:
- Reasoning should consider the closest prior art, well-known or commonly used art, and common general knowledge.
- Examiner evaluates whether claimed invention is selection of optimal material, mere design modification, mere aggregation, or whether closest prior art discloses a motivation/causal teaching to reach the claimed invention.
- Combining methods from different fields or applying methods to other fields is usually within ordinary creative activity unless technical difficulty (teaching-away) exists or special circumstances (remarkably advantageous effects) are shown.
- Problems to be solved (e.g., 'improve decision level using AI' or 'easier input via GUI') are considered as of filing.
- A person skilled in the art is expected to have common general knowledge of both the applied field and computer technology; may be regarded as a group rather than a single person.
- Examples of ordinary creativity include: applying techniques to other fields (file retrieval -> medical retrieval), adding commonly known means or equivalents, implementing hardware functions in software, systematizing human transactions using routine analysis/design methods, reproducing known events in virtual space, and design modifications based on known facts/customs.
- Effects such as faster processing, handling more data, reduced errors, or uniform results are general effects often resulting from computerization and are not usually unforeseeable; inventive step assessment takes these into account.
- Notes: commercial success can be evidence of inventive step if causally linked to claimed features; mere differences in data contents often do not confer novelty; recording a program/data on a storage medium or claiming a medium that merely transmits information are generally insufficient for inventive step/novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlarged Concept of Novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Application and scope of Article 29(3) (enlarged concept of novelty), conditions to meet its requirements and exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains when the enlarged concept applies, how to determine identicalness and special rules for international applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-to-File Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Purport and application of the first-to-file principle (Article 36), requirements for application and examination methods related to first-to-file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details on how filing dates govern rights, practical examination considerations and instructions to examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpatentable Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories of subject-matter that are unpatentable under Article 32 of the Patent Act and how to apply the statutory exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines unpatentable inventions and provides purport/interpretation guidance for examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of Specification, Claims or Drawings — Overview
rubrics_metrics.description: General provisions governing amendments including Article 47, purpose of amendment, requirements, and amendment periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies when voluntary amendments or amendments in response to rejections are allowed, timing limits and procedural steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Permissible Amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits on permissible amendments (voluntary or in reply to non-final rejection), amendments after amendment-triggered rejections and on reexamination requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines added-matter boundaries, when amendments will be refused, and how to assess whether an amendment changes the subject-matter beyond what was originally disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal to Enter Amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal basis (Articles 51 and 63) and requirements for refusing to enter an amendment, examination method and cautions for such refusal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural and substantive criteria examiners must apply when rejecting proposed amendments and the review process for refusals.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Examination Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall flow of patent examination: designation of examiner, classification assignment, laying open, request for examination, start of examination, processing deadlines and general principles for law application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides examiners through administrative steps, assignment, timing, and legal interpretive principles to apply during examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search for Prior Art
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and standards for searching prior art: overview, pre-search procedures, detailed search procedures, post-search measures, and outsourced prior art search institute usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies how to select search fields, databases, what constitutes an appropriate search, documentation of search results, and follow-up actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination Process (detailed steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed examiner tasks: understanding invention, reviewing prior art, handling special applications, issuing notice of grounds for rejection, instructions for written arguments, conducting additional searches, and making grant/reject decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes guidance on written argument handling, additional searches, interviews (personal interview procedures), amendments in response to final rejection, decision criteria and cancellation of examination measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and instructions for reexamination including overview and detailed reexamination process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines for conducting reexamination, interaction with appeal/review processes, and examiner obligations during reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Application Filed in a Language other than Korean
rubrics_metrics.description: Special rules for foreign-language filings: overview, treatment of new matters beyond foreign language/specification and Korean translations, correction of mistranslation and other considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How to handle discrepancies between original foreign-language specification and Korean translation, limits on adding new matter via translation and correction procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Applications — Divisional and Converted Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for divisional and converted applications: statutory basis, requirements for division/conversion, procedural steps, effects and examination of such applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains when division or conversion is allowed, required formalities and how these applications are examined and treated vis-à-vis parent filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority Claims (under treaty and domestic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements, procedures, effects, and amendment/examination of priority claims under international treaties and domestic priority claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed steps for claiming priority, evidence required, effects on novelty/priority date, and how priority claims are processed and amended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Term Extension and Other Post-Grant Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for patent term extension (e.g., for regulatory approval delays), period eligible, application/registration procedures, and examination for extension; and other post-grant procedures including extensions for delays in registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria for eligibility, documentation required, calculation of extension periods, and examination standards for such applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination on National Defense-related Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Special handling, procedures and confidentiality measures for national defense-related applications, including possible transfer to specialized bureaus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures for handling confidential documents, prohibition/permission of overseas filing and other security-related measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and procedures for expedited examination: relevant provisions, overview, objects eligible, and guidelines for determining expedited status by subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists categories eligible for expedited processing and instructions to examiners for assessing requests and prioritizing examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration by Examiners before Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure and requirements for internal reconsideration by examiners prior to appeal proceedings, including review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies eligibility for reconsideration, required materials, review steps, and examiner responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex-officio Re-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: System and requirements for ex-officio re-examination initiated by the office, including summary, requirements and notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the office may initiate re-examination, what triggers it, and special considerations for such internal reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positive Examination (suggesting amendments and pre-amendment communications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines encouraging proactive procedures such as suggesting amendments to applicants (positive examination), ex-officio amendments, pre-amendment communications, preliminary examination and other collaborative/constructive examination measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details methods to suggest amendments, target applications, inappropriate examples, ex-officio amendment scope & procedure, pre-amendment interview processes, and collective examination practices intended to reach allowance where possible without sacrificing legal standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and purposes for collective examination of applications (group handling/assessment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides overview and process steps for conducting collective examination sessions, and describes when collective examination is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination Criteria by Technology (technology-specific requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Technology-specific requirements and examination guidance for particular fields (biotech, pharmaceutical & cosmetics, food, functional drinking water, chemical compounds, alloy, polymers, textile, architectural design, computer-related inventions, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each technology chapter provides specific requirements for description and claims, patentability considerations, examples and special rules (e.g., sequences in biotech, data for food, unit conversions in textile, software/systemization guidance in computer-related inventions).
